_comment: CCV event schema -- the single source of truth for §1's per-instruction
event stream. tools/gen-event-schema.py generates the C++ header and the
SystemVerilog header from THIS FILE; neither is edited by hand, and §9's
requirement that names be mechanically consistent across the two languages
is satisfied by construction rather than by discipline.
WHAT IS AND IS NOT DECIDED HERE. §8 is explicit that the taxonomy is a
MECHANISM (Stage 1c) plus CONTENT that populates later, from two different
places: load-bearing events fall out of the Stage 2 interface grill-me,
arbitration-sensitive events per block at Stage 4a. So the events below are
a seed set, drawn only from the examples §1 itself names, and every one is
marked provisional. Closing the list is Stage 2's job and Stage 4a's, not
this file's.
The two CLASSES, by contrast, are decided, and the split is the point.
§1: load-bearing events must match exactly and any divergence is a bug;
arbitration-sensitive events are only comparable if the timing model's
arbiter is faithful to RTL's down to tie-break rules.

LOAD-BEARING CONTENT IS POPULATED by EV_CH_XFER plus the channel list in schema/interfaces.json. THE PRINCIPLE (Q-2): an event earns its place only if its timing is decided by an arbiter inside a block. Anything that is definitionally a channel transfer is already EV_CH_XFER on a named channel, and a duplicate that can drift is worse than no event. EV_RETIRE is the open case (Q-41).

TOLERANCE (Q-5): every event carries `tolerance`, reserved and null. The criterion is exact match. The key's PRESENCE is in the semantic hash; its VALUE is not, because a tolerance changes how two traces are compared, not how one is read. Setting one later therefore leaves every trace readable. tools/gen-event-schema.py refuses a non-null tolerance until Q-5 is reopened.

load_bearing.description: Architectural-state-affecting, or an interface transaction. Must match exactly between timing model and RTL; any divergence is a bug.

arbitration_sensitive.description: Outcome depends on an arbiter's algorithm including tie-breaks. Comparable only against a faithful arbiter model, not a statistically plausible one.
arbitration_sensitive.correlation: exact (Q-5). Achievable because Q-4 makes arbitration policy a specified input to both the timing model and the RTL rather than an implementation accident. A tolerance is the wrong default: it is where drift hides, and nobody ever tightens one.

units._comment: Track identifiers -- one track per block in the Perfetto view. DERIVED from params/blocks.json, which is the closed partition, rather than listed here: a second list would disagree with the first, and this one is read by every emit site. UNIT_UNKNOWN and UNIT_TESTBENCH are not blocks and are fixed at 0 and 1; block ids follow in the partition's order. Regenerating after a partition change renumbers them and moves the schema hash, which is the intended loud failure -- a trace captured under the old numbering must not silently read as the new one.

events.name: EV_DISPATCH
events.doc: ROB allocation in OOE: the cycle an instruction takes a reorder-buffer entry. Kept under Q-2's principle because that cycle is decided by OOE's allocation arbitration, internal to the block; the uop's arrival is ccv_dec_ooe_uop's EV_CH_XFER. Q-1 content: its final definition comes with OOE's Stage 4a.

events.name: EV_ISSUE
events.doc: Instruction is selected by the arbiter and issues. §1 names issue cycle as the canonical arbitration-sensitive event: an oldest-ready model and a priority-encoder tie-break diverge on every tie, permanently, and it looks exactly like a bug.

events.name: EV_WAKEUP
events.doc: An operand became ready. Paired with EV_ISSUE it gives §1's wakeup-to-issue latency.

events.name: EV_WARP_SELECT
events.doc: Two-tier SMT warp-select outcome, including which warps were eligible but not chosen -- a losing candidate is what makes a tie-break diff meaningful.

events.name: EV_RETIRE
events.doc: Instruction retires and commits architectural state. Arbitration-sensitive (Q-41, closed by the OOE session 2026-10-02): commit bandwidth is shared across the four tier-1 ROBs, so the cycle a warp retires is an arbiter's decision, as EV_DISPATCH's is. What ccv-sim's oracle is checked against is the per-warp retirement SEQUENCE, correlated separately (the kernel run's retire order), not this event's cycle.

events.name: EV_CH_XFER
events.doc: A transaction crossed a channel boundary. THE load-bearing event: §1 says decode, dispatch, retire and memory request/response ARE interface transactions, and the block-level grill-me made every one of them a credited channel. So the 40-channel list is the load-bearing event list, and one event type with the channel as a discriminator covers it -- emitted by the shared credit checker, so every boundary emits identically and no block can drift from the schema.

events.name: EV_ID_LINK
events.doc: An instruction is re-executed under a NEW id, linked to the old. Squash and replay are central to this machine -- branch recovery, load replay, demotion restore -- and a reused id would show one instruction with overlapping lifetimes instead of the replay. Arbitration-sensitive because whether a replay happens can depend on contention (load replay), so model and RTL may legitimately differ on it.

events.name: EV_OOE_GPR_EMPTY
events.doc: Rename blocks on a GPR with the free list empty. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_RENAME_LIMIT
events.doc: Rename blocks on another slot's floor or on this warp's ceiling. b: 0 floor, 1 ceiling; c: 0 GPR, 1 predicate. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_PRED_EMPTY
events.doc: Rename blocks on a predicate with the predicate free list empty. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_ROB_FULL
events.doc: The warp's ROB has no entry at rename. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_ROB_SLOT_HELD
events.doc: The next ROB slot is held by a squashed op still in flight (deferred free, OI-10). Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_RS_FULL
events.doc: A reservation-station class has no free entry at rename. b: 0 RCU class, 1 MIU class. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_RS_WARP_CAP
events.doc: The warp holds its reservation-station cap at rename. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_DECQ_FULL
events.doc: DEC is held: a uop stays in ccv_dec_ooe_uop with the decode queue full. a is the warp of the oldest held uop. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_DECQ_WARP_MAX
events.doc: A uop stays in the channel with its warp at its decode-queue maximum. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_CHWIDTH_HOLD
events.doc: Rename is held behind an in-flight chwidth change. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_BARRIER_HOLD
events.doc: Rename is held on a barrier wait. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_REDIRECT_BUSY
events.doc: A mispredict or epoch notice waits for the rate-1 redirect channel. b: redirects queued. Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_MEMOP_HELD
events.doc: A memop is ready but for an unconfirmed source while an MIU issue slot goes unused ("would have issued"). Per cycle: fires every cycle the condition holds, so its count is a duration. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_MEMOP_HOLD_CYCLES
events.doc: A memop issues; once per issue. c: cycles from all operands woken to issue. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_DEFERRED_FREE
events.doc: A squash leaves an entry holding its registers for an op still in flight (OI-10); once per such entry. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_READY_NOT_SELECTED
events.doc: An entry is ready and not issued; per cycle, per entry. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_CANCEL_REPLAY
events.doc: A withdrawn wake returns an issued entry to Waiting. c: depth from the missed load. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_DEMOTE_TRIGGER
events.doc: A demotion trigger crosses its threshold at the ROB head; once per head. b: 0 MLC miss, 1 barrier, 2 fallback timer; c: cycles the head has stalled. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_CROSS_GROUP_SQUASH
events.doc: A mispredict squashes entries of other PC groups; once per squash. OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

events.name: EV_OOE_COPY_ISSUE
events.doc: A masked load issues its copy-only op (CCV_OP_PRF_COPY, A-38). OOE's arbitration-sensitive set (register OI-7; docs/ooe-model.md, "Events owed to the schema").

_comment: Every event's instr_uid (interface decisions, 2026-09-24). TRACE-ONLY:
carried beside a message in a sideband that exists only under
CCV_TRACE, never in the RTL payload struct, so synthesis never sees it.
rob_tag cannot serve: it does not exist before rename, it is reused
after retirement, and the control channels have none.

seq.doc: 32-bit monotonic. instr: assigned at fetch. txn: the owning instruction's seq if `owned`, else from a separate transaction counter. none: 0.

sub.doc: Sub-index for one instruction's many transactions (a page-split access), so the view nests them under the instruction rather than showing peers. 0 = unnested.

owned.doc: txn only: seq names the owning instruction, and the transaction nests under it.

class.doc: What the id identifies; most channels are not per-instruction at all.

_retired_ids_comment: Ids of deleted events. Never reused: a reused id silently reinterprets every
trace already written. tools/gen-event-schema.py refuses one.
EV_BARRIER_RELEASE: deleted under Q-2. DECODE and the barrier pair were
exactly ccv_dec_ooe_uop, ccv_ooe_syu_bar and ccv_syu_ooe_rel. MEM_REQ and
MEM_RSP were ambiguous as well: one memop becomes several transactions
(MIU->SPM, MIU->DCU, DCU->MLC), each with its own req_id, which the per-hop
channel events carry. (EV_DECODE's text had also claimed to establish the
uid; the uid is created at fetch -- Q-3.)
